title: TGPO: Efficient Policy Optimization through Sequence Anchor and Information Gating
claim: Existing fine-grained and coarse-grained methods trade stability against efficiency; adaptively gating granularity by trust resolves the tension and yields both.
layout: 4 panels in a 2x2-ish grid, left-to-right flow, big arrows between panels
description: A four-panel composite with large blue arrows linking the panels. The top-left panel, titled 'The Stability-Efficiency Dilemma', contrasts GRPO (token-level learning, with one starred outlier token) and GSPO (a single sequence-level block) on a balance scale, with bullet lists of pros and cons. The top-middle panel, 'What Goes Wrong In Practice', shows a row of tokens in which one red token dominates the update (GRPO). It also shows a greyed sequence that is discarded into a trash can (GSPO). The bottom panel, 'Control the granularity of learning dynamically', shows a gradient slider from an anchor (sequence-level) to a flame (token-level). A blue dot marks TGPO's adaptive position. Trust-score inputs and a highlighted red callout sit below the slider. The right panel contrasts a tangled arrow bundle (before) with clean parallel wavy arrows (TGPO). Below them are three benefit icons with green up-arrows and a small training-curve plot.
caption: Overview of Trust-Gated Policy Optimization Policy optimization faces a stability–efficiency tradeoff: token-level updates are expressive but unstable, while sequence-level optimization is stable but wasteful. TGPO resolves this tension by adaptively controlling learning granularity, using token-level detail only when it is trustworthy and otherwise relying on a sequence-level anchor.
abstract: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an important paradigm for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of large language models, while it also involves a persistent tradeoff between optimization stability and learning efficiency. Token-level importance weighting supports fine-grained credit assignment, but it often introduces high variance and unstable parameter updates, whereas sequence-level optimization provides more stable learning dynamics while failing to fully exploit informative local signals. We introduce T rust- G ated P olicy O ptimization (TGPO), an efficient policy optimization framework that integrates two complementary mechanisms, namely sequence anchors and information gates . TGPO aligns token-wise updates with a stable sequence-level reference, which reduces the influence of extreme local likelihood fluctuations on the gradient, and a trust-based information gate adaptively modulates the contribution of token-level signals. By retaining and reweighting gradients from imperfect trajectories rather than excluding them, TGPO improves gradient utilization and sample efficiency while maintaining stable optimization behavior. Empirical results across seven mathematical reasoning datasets and multiple model scales show that TGPO consistently enhances learning efficiency and overall performance in outcome-supervised reinforcement learning settings.
